notes: PETTY CASH NOW CHARGES THE RIGHT PART OF THE BUSINESS. If you run a float for a branch, a department or a project, its spending used to land against the business as a whole rather than against that part of it — so the float's own report never showed what it had spent, and its budget never moved. A float must now be told what it belongs to, and the picker asks rather than quietly answering for you. Petty cash vouchers carry a Charge to unit and a project, filled in from the float as soon as you pick it. And the budget warning now measures the expense against the budget it will really post to. RECORDS YOU HAVE ALREADY POSTED ARE CORRECTED TOO. This update moves past reimbursements onto the part of the business that spent them. It changes nothing else — no amount, account, date or voucher link — and it can be undone exactly. Only unambiguous cases are corrected, and a reversal is always corrected together with the voucher it reverses. TAKE A BACKUP BEFORE UPDATING, AND ANOTHER AFTERWARDS. This release changes how some data is stored, so a backup taken beforehand would restore the older shape. The app will keep reminding you on the dashboard until you take a fresh one — Backup & Export, Back up now. CLOSE A FLOAT ON THE DAY IT CLOSED. Retiring a float now asks for the date the cash went back, as funding and reimbursement already did. Closing in January for a year that ended in December used to record the return in January and put the deposit in the wrong month's bank reconciliation. A PROPER RETIREMENT DOCUMENT. Before you reimburse a float, print the statement of what it has spent: every voucher, split correctly when one voucher covered two kinds of expense, with a new Analysis by expenditure head totalling the claim by account beside the reconciliation of cash in hand — then Retired by / Checked by / Approved by. Attach the receipts and get it signed before the money goes back. MONTH-END ASKS ABOUT YOUR FLOATS. The month-end checklist now lists any float still holding spending it has not accounted for, so you do not sign a month off over an uncleared cash box. Advisory only — carrying a float across a month end is normal. PRINTED REPORTS FIT THE PAGE PROPERLY AGAIN. Several reports printed at screen spacing and ran onto more sheets than they needed.
